function: p. 10-14: DRL experts output communication and sensing beamformers, active-RIS discrete phases and gains, power-splitting ratios and common rates; SCA-AO refines part of them to maximize energy efficiency.
system: p. 3, 14-15: downlink active RIS-assisted ISCPT with RSMA, 8-antenna BS, 2 single-antenna power-splitting users, 1 sensing target, 20-element active RIS (gain up to 2), 2.45 GHz.
method: p. 11-14: PPO-based mixture-of-experts DRL with smooth clipping (3 experts, offline training), Informer forecaster of channel-block duration, and hybrid activation with optimization experts.
data_channel: p. 13-15: simulated Rician fading (factor 4) with distance path loss and random node positions; synthetic exponential channel-block durations (10^6 blocks) for the forecaster; no external dataset.
test_conditions: p. 10, 14-17: offline training on random user and target positions; results on 12 channel blocks and sweeps over users, RIS elements, amplification and thresholds; no unseen-condition test stated.
baselines: p. 15-16: SCA-AO, traditional MoE with constant clipping, PPO, DDPG and a random policy (figure legends); LSTM versus the Informer forecaster (Table II).
metrics: p. 15-17: energy efficiency (bit/Hz/J), running time, forecaster MSE, MAE and MAR, beam pattern.
complexity: p. 10: SCA-AO order O(I((K+T)^{7/2} NT^{13/2})((K+T)^{3/2} N^{7/2})); p. 15-16: H-MoE running time 56.17% below SCA-AO, in normalized units.
q1_support: p. 14: "the small-scale fading follows a Rician fading with a Rician factor 4" with a custom distance path loss (Table I, p. 15); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 17: "Fig. 10 shows the achievable EE with different number of RIS phase shift elements N": the sweeps (pp. 16-18) are parameter sweeps and the paper never states that a trained model is tested in an unseen setting; the forecaster is tested on a held-out 20% of the same synthetic data (p. 13).
q3_support: p. 15: "the MoE-SCF outperforms the traditional MoE by 11.35% and significantly outperforms other DRL-based schemes" (legend of Fig. 6(a), page image: PPO, DDPG, random); p. 16: "H-MoE reduces 56.17% iteration time compared to SCA-AO with less than 3.1% performance loss" gives the non-learned optimization baseline.
q4_support: p. 10: "the total computational complexity" for solving P1 is O(I((K+T)^{7/2} NT^{13/2})((K+T)^{3/2} N^{7/2})); p. 15: "the average iteration time of the H-MoE is reduced by about 56.17% compared with the" presented SCA-AO.
q5_support: p. 13: "the dataset is generated according to (50)" is synthetic; no link, DOI or repository for code or data appears anywhere, and no public channel dataset is used.
notes: Area 5: beams, sensing matrix and RIS design serving sensing, communication and power transfer, and the more specific ISAC area wins over area 3. The DRL experts act on all optimization variables (p. 10); H-MoE reuses part of them to warm-start SCA-AO. PPO, DDPG and random baselines appear only in the figure legends of page 16, read from the page image. Table I (p. 15) lists a 2.45 GHz working frequency and also a 4 GHz carrier frequency.
